note: Rules this repository learned the hard way. Each one exists because the thing it forbids already happened once, silently.

rules.reason: Generated, committed and drift-gated. Change the source instead: schemas/ then `make generate`; the Go wire types in libs/wire then `make openapi`; the harness wire modules then `make contract-fixtures`. A hand edit is reverted by the next regeneration and fails CI in the meantime.
§0-§9 are cited from code, schemas and tests. Renumbering silently breaks every `contract §N` citation in the tree.

This is the boundary of what is collected from real people. The keystroke channel carries timing and a coarse class only — never the key, never the field value. A widening here is a change to what the project is, and the consent text was false once already.
The six numbers are the project's central claim. Moving one requires a fresh manifest AND re-reading the prose around it — a re-baselined figure with stale prose is a document that now lies.
These freeze the exact bytes clients receive. Regenerating them is a deliberate act (`-update`) and must be called out in the PR; an accidental regeneration hides a contract change.

google.golang.org/protobuf is an archive-format pin, not a dependency: canonical bytes are hashed for content-addressed identity, so a bump is an archive-compatibility event. Dependabot is configured to leave it alone.
Every CI step must stay `run: make <target>`. Job names are required status checks — renaming one silently removes the protection. No sync gate may use `git status`.
Secret-bearing files. Reading one into a transcript leaks it; ~/.npmrc is on this list because that has happened.
